title: Service Hours, Holiday Schedules, and Operational Calendar Management for Vehicle Inspection Programs
capability_statement:
Parsons operates state vehicle inspection programs against agency-defined hours of operation, holiday calendars, and after-hours availability commitments, and treats schedule discipline as a measured service-level obligation rather than a best-effort target. On a current decentralized I/M program, Parsons and its call-center partner Dasher staff the station-operator and customer-service hotlines on the agency's normal business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. EST), answering 80% of calls within 20 seconds and 100% within a minute (well inside the agency's average-wait SLA of no more than four minutes), with help-desk service downtime contractually capped at 0.5% excluding pre-scheduled maintenance or agency-approved downtime, and 99.9% phone-system uptime achieved through automatic backup and failover systems, redundant circuits, multiple Internet connections and carriers, and 24/7/365 proactive support (chunks 2188, 2189).

For 24/7 calendar coverage, the production VIID and inspection-system stack run on a 24-hours-a-day, 7-days-a-week, every-year service basis on AWS, architected so that most maintenance and upgrades can be performed with no downtime and no impact on end users, including I/M stations performing inspections (chunk 2088). Custom-built scripts provide proactive warning of system issues so the team can act before a problem occurs, monitoring servers, network traffic, databases, and applications using performance thresholds; scheduled and unscheduled downtime are tracked separately, and Parsons reports all system downtime incidents to the agency at the time of the incident in addition to providing a monthly report (chunk 2090). Self-service kiosks operate 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, including on State-observed holidays, while expanded self-service tablet solutions inside inspection facilities are available during facility operating hours; inspection stations adhere to and observe the same holiday schedule and regular office closing schedule as the State Motor Vehicle agency, with all customer vehicles on station property at the time of closing inspected (no motorist turned away) (chunks 3835, 3836).

Program, audit, and hearing schedules are managed under a published, change-controlled calendar. The proposed work plan and program schedule are delivered as a Gantt chart in Attachment C, with start and completion dates for each task and durations in days; the Gantt chart is the primary tool for tracking program progress and is referenced in weekly progress meetings during the implementation phase, the agency retains final approval of the proposed draft schedule, and any deviations from the established timeline are documented and mitigated under a defined change-management process (chunks 1960, 2045, 2046). Audits are scheduled by published criteria (date of last audit, record-audit data analysis, consumer complaints, covert audit results, and agency requests); Parsons performs two unannounced overt audits per station per year during normal business hours regardless of station location, plus the equivalent of two covert audits per station per year, with Michael Baker International providing third-party validation of covert audit volume (chunks 2128, 2152). Hearing examiners schedule agency-requested administrative hearings within 14 days of notice and hold them within 30 days; expedited hearings are scheduled to agency-defined time frames; immediate-suspension hearings are scheduled within three days of suspension; and monthly reports document hearings scheduled, canceled, continued, held, and no-shows, plus suspensions served, appeals filed, and warning letters sent (chunks 2198, 2201, 2202, 2206).

Schedule discipline extends to data exchange, transition, and on-road testing. Parsons updates vehicle I/M information on the agency's registration and titling system to a schedule determined by the agency, and modifies its data feeds when the agency alters its modernization timeline (chunk 2098). Customer complaints route through a referee program: a hotline representative gathers information, forwards it to the appropriate regional office, and a Parsons team member contacts the customer to schedule a referee inspection at the original I/M station or, if refused, at another I/M station (chunk 2177). Remote-Sensing-Device data collection runs on a published timeline (3 weeks of data collection at approved on-road sites, analysis 4 weeks following data collection, reporting in conjunction with the Annual Report) using HEAT's EDAR technology to deliver a minimum of 20,000 valid RSD test results annually (chunks 2212, 2221, 2224). For State-set transition windows, Parsons proposes performing weekend and night facility work under a formal schedule developed by its proposed MBE General Contractor and approved by the State, with major transition items completed no later than 15 months following NTP and a Three-Day Inspection Program Station Mobilization that brings nearly 100 people on-site for the week of and the week following go-live (chunks 3678, 3682, 3692, 3693, 3694, 3709, 3710, 3753). Self-Acceptance-Test (SAT) demonstrations are prepared for completion within 45 days of the operational start of the entire testing network, with any unsatisfactory result addressed within 48 hours and scheduled for a retest (chunks 3755, 3757, 3759). Spare-part reorders take less than 72 hours to fulfill under an application-controlled maintenance schedule that identifies potential hardware failures (chunk 3827). For State notification during emergencies, the program-management team establishes immediate, direct communications via text messaging, email, and mobile and home phone numbers; on the New Jersey vehicle inspection program, Parsons created ParText, an all-in-one bulk SMS service for sending bulk alerts (chunk 3850). Customer feedback (positive and negative) is fully documented and captured electronically in the VID portal, with the Program Manager providing all feedback reporting and complaints to the agency at regularly scheduled meetings (chunk 3863).

differentiators:
- **Calendar-aware operations playbook**: Parsons treats hours of operation, holiday observance, and after-hours coverage as published, monitored service obligations. Inspection stations adhere to and observe the same holiday and regular-closing schedule as the State Motor Vehicle agency, with no motorist turned away after closing because vehicles already on station property are inspected (chunks 3835, 3836).
- **24/7 production with low-impact maintenance windows**: AWS-hosted architecture is engineered so most maintenance and upgrades occur with no downtime and no impact on stations performing inspections; custom-built monitoring scripts provide proactive warning before problems occur, and any incident is reported to the agency at the time it occurs (chunks 2088, 2090).
- **Separation of scheduled, unscheduled, and agency-approved downtime in reporting**: Monthly availability reports separately identify scheduled-maintenance downtime, agency-approved downtime, and unscheduled downtime, eliminating ambiguity in service-credit and SLA enforcement (chunks 2090, 2188, 2189).
- **Change-managed program schedule**: Gantt-based work plan delivered as Attachment C with start, completion, and duration tracking, weekly progress reviews during implementation, agency retains final approval of the draft schedule, and a defined change-management process documents and mitigates any deviation before the calendar slips (chunks 1960, 2045, 2046).
- **Audit and hearing calendars driven by published criteria**: Audits scheduled on documented inputs (date of last audit, record-audit analysis, complaints, covert results, agency requests) with third-party audit-volume validation by Michael Baker International; hearings scheduled to defined day-count targets (14/30/3 days) with monthly reporting on scheduled, canceled, continued, and held volumes (chunks 2128, 2152, 2198, 2202, 2206).
- **Pre-prepared transition with weekend/night work scheduling**: 18 named Parsons leads and nearly 100 people staged for the Three-Day Station Mobilization; weekend and overnight demolition/facility upgrades under a formal MBE-General-Contractor schedule approved by the State, with all major transition items completed no later than 15 months following NTP (chunks 3678, 3692, 3693, 3753).
- **Self-service after-hours access**: External self-service kiosks operate 24x7 including on State-observed holidays so motorists can transact outside facility hours; expanded in-facility self-service tablet solutions are available during operating hours (chunks 3835, 3836).
- **Multi-channel State emergency communication**: ParText bulk SMS service originated on the New Jersey program, plus text/email/mobile/home-phone direct lines to the agency, ensures stakeholders understand any impact on Inspection Program opening when hours differ from State Motor Vehicle agency branch hours (chunk 3850).
- **Workforce flexibility supports schedule resilience**: Parsons' "People First" culture, flexible work schedule, engineer "work-from-anywhere" program, and dual technical career path (chunk 3557) supply a workforce able to flex to State-defined schedule changes.
- **Customer-feedback loop on agency cadence**: All comments (positive and negative) captured in the VID portal; the Program Manager delivers feedback reports and complaints to the agency at regularly scheduled meetings (chunk 3863).
gap_notes:
- **A-022 (Annual political-contribution disclosure with the New Jersey ELEC)**: The provided evidence does not include any reference to political-contribution disclosure filings or ELEC paperwork. Capture team must source the corporate compliance attestation directly from Parsons' contracts/compliance organization.
- **R-058 / R-059 (Adhere to State holiday changes; obtain SCM pre-approval for unscheduled closings)**: The evidence shows Parsons operating against an agency-defined holiday calendar (chunks 3835, 3836) and confirms the team understands the difference between scheduled and unscheduled downtime (chunk 2090), but no chunk describes a specific pre-approval workflow for unscheduled station closings tied to severe weather or emergencies routed through SCM. Capture team should commit to a documented unscheduled-closing notification and pre-approval procedure.
- **A-066 (Six PIF/PFF seminars in different geographic regions during Implementation Phase)**: The evidence does not describe a multi-region implementation-phase seminar series for inspection-station owners or operators. Capture team must develop a seminar plan (locations, dates, agenda, registration mechanism).
- **A-070 / A-071 (Delayed payment plan as part of PIF/PFF Support Plan; 24/7 automated response system for non-business hours)**: The evidence describes the 24x7 VIID and a daytime-staffed help desk (chunks 2088, 2188), but does not specifically describe an automated IVR or self-service response system for routine after-hours inquiries; the help desk is staffed but not described as 24/7 automated. Capture team should commit to deploying an after-hours IVR for routine requests or source proof of an existing 24/7 IVR deployment, and produce a delayed-payment plan tied to the PIF/PFF Support Plan.
- **A-042 (Section 4.34.3 — comprehensive documentation per SLA schedule)**: The evidence describes monthly reporting on availability, help-desk activity, hearings, and audits (chunks 2090, 2188, 2189, 2206), but does not enumerate the specific documentation deliverables listed under the agency's SLA schedule. Capture team should map each SLA-schedule deliverable to an existing or new monthly/quarterly artifact.
- **All Article-II through Article-XXXV requirements (collective-bargaining-agreement schedule and leave provisions)**: Items A-011 (membership cure within 10 days), A-029 (Union-meeting schedule adjustments), A-068 / A-057 / A-059 (Saturday and weekday overtime caps and drafted-shift pay), A-042 (steward super-seniority), A-005 / A-009 / A-011 (layoffs and bumping), A-020 (Part-Time recall), A-021 (5-working-day vacancy posting), A-041 (Saturday hours 5-8 hours), A-046 (Senior Lane Tech lunch/break scheduling), A-033 (workweek schedules posted one month in advance), A-034 (one-hour unpaid lunch and four 15-minute paid breaks for technical/material/ERT), M-003 / A-014 / A-015 (sick/vacation/jury/civilian-duty leave), A-059 / A-064 / A-065 (vacation accrual mechanics), and A-039 (Step 2 grievance presentation within 10 calendar days) are CBA-driven scheduling and leave provisions. The provided evidence is from inspection-program technical submittals and the corporate dossier and contains no collective-bargaining-agreement language, workforce-scheduling artifacts, or grievance-procedure documentation. Capture team must source these from Parsons HR / Labor Relations and from any incumbent-workforce transition plan.
- **R-018 (Allow State research during normal operations)**: No chunk specifically describes a procedure for accommodating in-person State research at stations or in operations centers. Capture team should add an explicit research-cooperation commitment.
- **R-039 (Adhere to Contract Schedule)**: While the Gantt-based program schedule, weekly progress reviews, and change-management process (chunks 1960, 2045, 2046) collectively support adherence, the proposal team should still extract the State's specific Contract Schedule milestones from the RFP and reflect them verbatim in the response.
